Ethereum is a decentralised blockchain platform that provides a framework for creating and executing smart contracts and decentralised applications (dapps).
Conceived by Vitalik Buterin in 2013 and launched in 2015, Ethereum was developed to extend the functionality of blockchain technology beyond simple value transfers by introducing programmability.
At the heart of Ethereum is the Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM), an execution environment that processes smart contracts, ensuring that code runs exactly as written without central oversight.
This design enables developers to build applications that operate in a trustless and transparent manner, serving use cases in areas such as finance, digital identity, and supply chain management.
Ether (ETH), the native cryptocurrency of the platform, is used to pay for network operations like gas fees and to support the incentives that maintain the network's security.
By facilitating these essential functions, Ether underpins both routine transactions and the broader engagement of participants within the ecosystem.
ETH also serves as a key trading asset on cryptocurrency exchanges, enabling users to trade or invest in various digital assets and participate actively in decentralized finance (DeFi) markets.
Ethereum’s open-source nature and its active global development community drive ongoing protocol improvements.
This continuous evolution supports a wide range of applications and positions Ethereum as a key platform in the landscape of decentralised technology.
Ethereum operates by recording a continuous series of transactions in blocks that update the network's overall state.
Each block includes transactions that either transfer Ether between accounts or execute smart contracts, with the Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM) ensuring that every instruction is carried out precisely as written.
The network utilizes a dual account model: externally owned accounts (controlled by private keys) and contract accounts (governed by code).
However, following the Pectra upgrade in 2025, regular accounts gained the ability to temporarily function as smart contracts during transactions.
This "Smart Account" functionality enables advanced features like transaction batching and sponsored gas fees directly from standard wallets.
A core component of Ethereum’s functionality is its Proof of Stake consensus mechanism.
In this model, validators stake Ether to propose and confirm new blocks.
While the minimum stake to run a solo validator remains 32 ETH, recent upgrades have raised the maximum effective balance to 2,048 ETH, allowing large operators to consolidate their stake and reduce network strain.

Farside data show a $99.9 million net withdrawal on Thursday, November 5.
The flow data cannot establish a direct forecast for ETH's price.
The November 5 figure is not a reliable prediction of ETH's next move.

TL;DR: US spot Ether ETFs posted a $99.9 million net outflow on November 5, Farside data show, following an $85.3 million outflow on November 3 and a temporary recovery on November 4.
The pattern highlights a fragile demand picture, but cannot establish a direct forecast for ETH’s price.
Ether’s exchange-traded fund market is still searching for consistency.
The latest fully reported daily figures in Farside Investors’ Ether ETF table show a $99.9 million net withdrawal on Thursday, November 5, just a day after the same group recorded a $53 million inflow.
The reversal demonstrates why single-session data need context.
November 6’s table still contained unreported fields when reviewed, so it would be misleading to present the partial figure as a final market-wide total.
A dated, complete session offers a better basis for an editorial assessment.
On November 5, BlackRock’s ETHA recorded a $75.2 million outflow and the firm’s ETHB line showed a further $22 million leaving.
Fidelity’s FETH was down $2.2 million, while Grayscale’s ETHE showed a modest $500,000 withdrawal.
Those figures add up to the $99.9 million negative session.
The previous day looked different.
On November 4, the listed products collectively brought in $53 million, with positive flows in several funds offsetting negative readings elsewhere.
Before that, November 2 and 3 brought losses of $139.7 million and $85.3 million respectively.
The emerging picture is not a perfectly uninterrupted exodus.
It is a market in which intermittent buying has yet to overcome repeated bouts of selling.
Our earlier report on November 2’s Ether ETF withdrawals provides a useful baseline.
The subsequent sessions show that the pressure has persisted but has also varied substantially between days and issuers.
An ETF’s reported flow measures changes in the investment wrapper, not all Ethereum transactions.
Institutions can obtain ETH exposure through spot holdings, derivatives, treasury companies and other vehicles.
A negative day in the US listed fund category does not prove every sophisticated investor has turned bearish.
This is especially important for Ethereum because a significant share of the network’s economic activity occurs independently of an ETF.
Stablecoin transfers, decentralised exchanges, tokenised assets and staking continue to operate whatever happens to a particular fund’s share count.
The long-term investment case for ETH is often tied to that activity, but there is no automatic formula linking application usage to the token’s short-term price.
Concentration adds another layer.
If one manager dominates the day’s net withdrawals, the aggregate should not be described as a consensus of all issuers.
Analysts also need to separate price moves from flows: the dollar value of assets in a fund can fall because of market prices even when investors have not redeemed an equivalent amount of shares.
The first is whether ETF investors return in size and for more than a single session.
The second is what happens in Ethereum’s development roadmap.
The Ethereum Foundation announced a Glamsterdam testing delay on November 6, citing concerns about how proposed gas changes could affect existing applications.
That is an engineering issue, not proof of a market-flow response, and it should be covered on its own terms.
For traders and longer-term holders, the practical takeaway is to compare several fully reported sessions, assess which issuers are driving the moves and resist treating flows as a stand-alone trading signal.
Thursday’s number is meaningful evidence of weaker demand through US funds; it is not a reliable prediction of ETH’s next move.

What Is XRP / XRP Ledger?
Who Are the Founders of the XRP Ledger?
What Makes XRPL Unique?
The XRP Ledger presents a wide variety of applications and use cases related to payments including micropayments, DeFi, and, soon, NFTs.
Deployed in 2012, the XRPL supports enterprises and Python, Java and JavaScript developers with powerful utility and flexibility.
On the XRP website, developers can access different tutorials to help them get started using different coding languages, building apps, managing accounts and more.
Alongside its native coin, XRP, the XRP Ledger is used by developers to create solutions that solve inefficiencies, including remittance and asset tokenization.
Currently, the five main applications of the XRP Ledger are payments, tokenization, DeFi, CBDCs and stablecoins.
How Many XRP Coins Are There in Circulation?
How Is the XRP Ledger Network Secured?
Unlike Bitcoin or Ethereum, the XRPL uses a unique Federated Consensus mechanism as its method of validating transactions.
Transactions are confirmed on the XRPL through a consensus protocol, in which designated independent servers called validators come to an agreement on the order and outcome of XRP transactions.
All servers in the network process each transaction according to the same rules, and any transaction that follows the protocol is confirmed right away.
All transactions are public and transparent, and anyone can operate a validator.
There are currently over 150 validators on the ledger, operated by universities, exchanges, businesses, and individuals around the world.
Through the Federated Consensus mechanism, all verified transactions can be processed without a single point of failure as no single participant makes a decision independently.

Ripple and the SEC
Since late 2020, Ripple Labs, which uses the XRP token in its products, has been locked in a legal battle with the United States Securities and Exchange Commission.
The big question is whether or not XRP is a security.
On Dec.
22, 2020, the SEC filed a lawsuit against Ripple Labs and two of its executives on the grounds that they traded $1.3 billion in their XRP token as security without registering it with the commission.
There have been arguments for and against the lawsuit.
However, Ripple has strongly countered the claims, arguing that the SEC has been biased in its assessment.
The SEC uses the “Howey test,” based on the Supreme Court ruling on SEC v.
W.J.
Howey Co in 1946, to determine whether a cryptocurrency is a security.
An asset is considered a security if it is sold with the expectation of getting profits from the efforts of other parties.
Based on the commission’s definition of XRP in its lawsuit, the cryptocurrency would pass the Howey test, and according to SEC regulations, all securities must be registered.
While most companies targeted by the SEC in a similar matter chose to settle, Ripple decided to fight.
The outcome of the lawsuit will undoubtedly have far-reaching implications in the crypto space.
If Ripple prevails, the SEC could lose some of its credibility, giving other crypto-based companies the confidence to revolt.
On the flip side, if the SEC wins the case, it could upend the way crypto firms operate and usher in a new wave of registration rules that apply to securities.

Ethereum is a blockchain platform that enables developers to build and deploy smart contracts and decentralized applications, operating through thousands of independent nodes worldwide rather than through a central authority.

What Is the Difference Between Ethereum and Ether (ETH)?
-
Ethereum is the network.
It is the decentralized, global blockchain platform that runs smart contracts and supports applications.
Think of it as a global computer or an operating system.
-
Ether (ETH) is the cryptocurrency.
It is the native token or "fuel" of the Ethereum network.

Ether is the asset that is bought, sold, and traded on exchanges.
How Does Ethereum Work?
Ethereum operates as a global, decentralized computer that executes programs called smart contracts.
The network consists of thousands of independent nodes operated by individuals and organizations worldwide, all maintaining a shared record of transactions and data.
When someone initiates a transaction or interacts with an application on Ethereum, validators process and confirm these actions, adding them to the blockchain permanently.
Unlike traditional centralized systems where a single entity controls operations, Ethereum distributes authority across its entire network.
This design ensures that no single party can manipulate transactions or shut down applications.
The network's native cryptocurrency, ether, serves multiple purposes: it pays for transaction fees, compensates validators for securing the network, and functions as collateral in various financial applications.

Smart contracts are self-executing programs stored on the Ethereum blockchain that automatically carry out agreements when specific conditions are met.
Written primarily in Solidity, a programming language designed for Ethereum, these contracts run on the Ethereum Virtual Machine, which acts as a global computing platform distributed across thousands of nodes.
The EVM ensures that smart contracts execute identically on every computer in the network, creating a trustworthy environment where outcomes are predictable and tamper-proof.
Developers can build anything from simple payment systems to complex financial instruments, gaming platforms, and decentralized organizations.
Once deployed, smart contracts operate autonomously without the need for intermediaries, and their code remains publicly verifiable on the blockchain.
This programmability distinguishes Ethereum from Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies focused solely on transferring value.
Applications built on Ethereum can hold and transfer assets, enforce rules, manage identities, and coordinate activities between multiple parties without traditional intermediaries like banks, brokers, or administrators.

The network randomly selects validators to create blocks and confirm transactions based on their staked amount and other factors.
Validators earn rewards for honestly performing their duties but face penalties, known as slashing, if they act maliciously or fail to maintain their nodes properly.
This economic incentive structure ensures network security without requiring massive computational power.
A validator who attempts to approve fraudulent transactions or goes offline repeatedly risks losing a portion of their staked ether.

Bitcoin dropped toward $74,000 on Tuesday after Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said policymakers need to follow through on anticipated rate hikes to preserve their credibility.
He suggested that a bigger half-percentage-point increase might be appropriate in December.
Speaking in London on Tuesday, Waller said he is leaning toward a December rate hike regardless of whether October inflation eases.
The consumer price index, due out this morning, is expected to show prices rising 0.3% for the month and 0.2% for core.
If inflation is hotter than forecast, Waller said he would support more robust action, including considering a 50 basis point hike at the December meeting.
He cautioned that a 25 basis point increase in that scenario would put the Fed’s credibility on the line, a risk he does not want to take.
Waller said markets had already priced in additional hikes because of Fed communications around the October meeting.
In his view, the crucial point is that those hikes are eventually delivered, without needing to occur at consecutive meetings.
Failing to act, he warned, would cause markets to pare back rate expectations and send rates lower immediately, effectively loosening policy in an undesirable way.
He said higher rates would be required sooner rather than later, stressing that the timing is less important than ensuring the promised hikes are carried out within a reasonable period.

Following the news that Hamas had invaded Israel, many were looking to the White House to make some sort of statement about the events and what their response would be.
Instead, the White House announced that it was calling a lid on Oct.
9, 2023, a term that may have been confusing to some who weren't familiar with it.
Of course, the idea of calling a lid isn't new in the world of politics, but it's a term that's specific to politicians' work.
Given that the term is only used in that specific context, many naturally wondered what it means and why it's used so frequently in politics.
What does it mean to call a lid?
When the White House announces that it's calling a lid, it's a signal to those in the news media that there will be no more news coming out of the White House that day.
In essence, it means that there will be no additional press briefings or photo opportunities.
Lids are often called in the White House when something urgent is demanding the attention of the entire staff, leaving them with little time to talk to press.
Presidential campaigns can also call a lid, and it has the same meaning in that context.
It can also be called a "full lid."
Crucially, though, calling a lid doesn't necessarily mean that the candidate or president is done working for the day, or that nothing newsworthy is going to happen.
All it means is that reporters can fairly safely leave the White House or turn their attention to other stories.
There are also rare circumstances where a lid may get lifted because of a major news event that happens after one is called.
The White House calls a lid in order to ensure that it's able to do delicate work without the media around.
Although it's the White House's job to keep the media, and thereby the public, informed, calling a lid allows them to temporarily build a wall allows them to work quicker and secretly.
The term was popularized by 'The West Wing.'
Although the idea of calling a lid has been around for decades, it was actually popularized by the character C.J.
Cregg on The West Wing, who was the show's press secretary.
Given the often dramatic events in that show, she had numerous opportunities to call a lid throughout the show's run.
On Oct.
9, the Biden White House called a lid because of the ongoing crisis in Israel.
This doesn't mean that there will never be any announcements about the crisis, just that there wouldn't be one that day.

十月 token 用量增长 37%
我们对上个月 AI 亮点的分析。token 用量飙升，每 token 价格持续下降，智能体流量现已占 OpenRouter 所处理流量的大部分。
亮点
- token 用量持续增长： 较 9 月增长 37%，达到 1 月的近 25 倍。
- 每 token 的实际价格下降： 每 token 的混合平均价格持续下降，上个月比 1 月平均水平低 57% 至 70%。
- 决策模型目前占所有请求的 21%： 尽管这一类别才出现数周，决策模型目前的请求量已超过文本模型以外的任何模态。
10 月共 790 万亿 token
10 月是 OpenRouter 历史上规模最大的月份：token 用量达到 790T，较 9 月增长 37%，更达到 1 月的惊人 25 倍。
此次增长覆盖广泛，但 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 的更新，以及 Haiku 5.5 和 Claude 5.5 系列其余模型的推出，是主要推动因素。
智能体消耗了全部 token 的 76%
智能体的主导地位在 2026 年持续增强。我们使用一个对七项信号加权的分类器，将每个 API 密钥归类为智能体驱动、人类驱动或混合类型，这些信号包括工具调用率、对话轮数和请求时间分布。
一年前，智能体密钥占 token 用量的 8%。十月，这一占比达到 76%，约为 600T token。
智能体使用的一个显著特点是每轮都会重新发送相同且通常很长的上下文，因此提示词缓存对智能体比对人类使用更为重要。十月，大多数提供商通过缓存前缀处理了智能体提示词 token 的 85% 至 97%。缓存命中率中位数大幅上升，从六月的 76.1% 升至十月的 90% 以上。
开放权重模型回升
在 9 月 28 日当周，开放权重模型在付费 token 中的占比降至 52%，当时 Claude Opus 5.5、 Sonnet 5.5 和 GPT-6.1 Sol 均已发布。两周后，该占比回升至 70% 以上，主要得益于 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash。
开放权重模型约占付费支出的四分之一，高于一月的 11%，且这一占比在过去一个季度左右几乎没有变化。
自一月以来，每 token 的实际价格下降了 57 至 70%
闭源权重模型的每百万 token 综合价格从 $1.21 降至 $0.52，开放权重模型则从 $0.28 降至 $0.084。两者之间的价差从 4.3× 扩大至 6.2×。
这一实际价格可能因多种因素而变化：模型的标价、模型组合本身，或每个会话的缓存命中率。8 月闭源模型价格的下降主要源于组合变化： GPT-5.6 Luna 以每百万 token 约 0.07 美元的价格，在发布后的几天内成为使用量最大的付费闭源模型。
各实验室模型份额
通常，各实验室的流量集中在少数几个模型上，而最新发布的模型通常会在一个月内占据主导地位。选择一个实验室，查看其 token 和支出构成在这一年中的变化。
开放权重模型实验室在增长方面领先
自五月以来， Z.ai 的月度 token 用量增长至约二十倍，而 DeepSeek 的月度 token 用量增长至约十二倍。在支出方面，Z.ai 的支出增长至约六倍， Anthropic 的支出增长了 76%，而 MiniMax 的支出下降了 20%，尽管其 token 用量大幅增长。
各家实验室的增长很少呈线性。随着模型发布竞争日益激烈，新模型的发布时间可能让实验室在单个月内的增长出现剧烈变化。
任务排行榜突出展示了两个模型
我们将抽样请求归入我们 排行榜 页面上的任务类别。按 token 用量统计，DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 在大多数编程和智能体任务中领先。切换到支出统计后，Claude Opus 5.5 在榜单的大多数类别中领先。
其他上榜模型包括 Jev 1.13，这款决策模型来自 TypeSafe，以及 GLM 5.3 Flash，后者在数据提取和数据转换中均表现强劲。
闭源权重实验室（以及 DeepSeek）在用户留存率方面领先
衡量模型或实验室的留存率有多种方式。这里，我们选取了在某个月向某个实验室的模型发送至少 100 次付费请求的账户，并检查其中有多少在下个月再次使用了同一实验室的模型。该门槛过滤掉了一次性试用，而在更低和更高的门槛下，各实验室的排名也非常相近。
从九月到十月， Google 保留了其中 78% 的账户，Anthropic 为 74%， OpenAI 为 74%。领先的开放权重模型实验室的月度留存率往往较低，十月也不例外。
决策模型的请求占比达到 21%
决策模型（按 TypeSafe 的命名方式称为 System One 模型）用于判断范围明确的问题，例如路由、内容审核或是非检查。它们在九月中旬才成为一个类别，到十月 26 日所在周就已占所有请求的 21%。
这里的文本模型指向 Chat Completions API 发出的所有请求，包括带有图像输入的请求。如果按 token 或支出而非请求数计算，决策模型在每周流量中所占的比例会小得多。
开放权重模型推理提供商：Together 升至首位
在提供开放权重模型的提供商中， Together 按提供的 token 总量计，从六月的第十八名升至十月的第一名。 DeepSeek 在九月跌至第九名，并凭借 V4.1 Flash 重返第二名，而 InferenceNet 跻身前十，位列第四。
我们每周都会分析这个千万亿级 token 数据池中的关键趋势。订阅 Inferred（我们的数据通讯），即可在收件箱中直接收到我们所有的重要研究报告。
方法说明
- 数据涵盖 2026 年 1 月 1 日至 10 月 31 日通过 OpenRouter API 发出的请求；智能体图表从 2025 年 9 月开始。周度图表以周一为每周的起始日。
- token 数为提示 token 数与补全 token 数之和。支出为已计费用量。实验室指模型开发者，模型权重公开发布即为开放权重模型。
- 每个 API 密钥每月都会根据七项加权信号进行分类：工具调用率、输入输出比、每次请求的轮数、缓存命中率、每次请求提供的工具数、请求间隔和取消率。得分为 0.50 或以上归为智能体使用，0.25 至 0.49 归为混合使用，低于 0.25 归为人类使用。
- 付费流量不包括免费模型变体。
- 实际价格、缓存命中率和提供商排名不包含自带密钥（BYOK）流量和隐身模型。缓存命中率是智能体密钥流量中已缓存提示 token 占提示 token 的比例，仅统计当月智能体 token 至少达到 1T 的提供商。
- 各任务的领先模型基于请求样本得出，这些样本按排行榜任务分类体系进行分类，并按采样率加权。
- 留存统计涵盖每月向某实验室模型发送至少 100 次付费请求的账户，若账户在次月向该实验室发送过任何付费请求，则视为留存账户。被封禁的账户不计入统计。
- 决策模型指发送到 decisions API 的请求。文本模型指发送到 Chat Completions API 的请求，包括带有图像输入的请求。

DeepSeek updates AI model, intensifying competition with Anthropic and OpenAI
Photo: Google DeepMind / Pexels
The Hangzhou startup's V4.1-Flash-1017 update is billed as faster and leaner, with benchmark gains and unchanged API pricing
DeepSeek has shipped another update to its AI lineup, and this one is built around a familiar pitch: more performance for less money.
The Hangzhou-based startup released DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 on October 17, 2026.
It is designed to be faster and leaner as it competes with Silicon Valley heavyweights like OpenAI and Anthropic, plus a growing crowd of Chinese rivals.
The timing matters.
The model it replaces only arrived on September 10, 2026, so this refresh landed roughly five weeks later.
What changed in the new model
DeepSeek describes the update as a “Pareto improvement” in both performance and cost.
That economics term means one thing gets better without anything else getting worse.
Applied here, the model is reported to post stronger benchmark scores, finish tasks faster and produce shorter outputs.
API pricing stays the same, and developers reach the model through the existing deepseek-flash endpoint.
Shorter outputs may sound like a minor detail.
They are not, because AI usage is typically billed by the volume of text a model generates.
A model that reaches the same answer in fewer words is cheaper to run, even when the sticker price does not move.
The headline benchmark figure comes from DeepSWE v1.1, a coding test.
The new model scored 77.0%, up from 74.2% for the previous version.
Benchmarks indicate that figure also tops Claude Opus 5 from Anthropic, which scored 74.0%.
Benchmarks further suggest DeepSeek outperforms larger models, Claude Opus 5 among them, on reasoning and coding tasks.

Join 34,000+ readers across crypto, finance, and policy.
Cost is where the gap looks widest.
Effective per-task costs for DeepSeek’s model are often under $0.20-$0.25, compared with $2-$10+ for competitor models.
Agents, coding and a new set of APIs
Much of the improvement centers on what the industry calls agentic capability.
DeepSeek says it strengthened these agentic and coding skills using reinforcement learning with self-feedback.
The practical upshot is end-to-end project building.
Users can reportedly ask the model to create things like games and 3D models, not just snippets of code.
The update also expands what DeepSeek sells.
For the first time, the company is opening its Search & Fetch APIs to outside developers.
Those tools are priced at $0.75 per 1,000 calls.
Some of them are being offered free until November 1, 2026.
The model itself is available on DeepSeek’s website, app and API.
Its weights are open-sourced under the MIT license on platforms including Hugging Face and ModelScope.
Background: a faster release cadence
DeepSeek has been picking up speed throughout 2026.
Since mid-year, the company has moved to monthly updates, with a consistent focus on efficient architectures and open weights.
That strategy sets it apart from its biggest US competitors.
OpenAI and Anthropic largely keep their most advanced model weights closed and sell access through paid products and APIs.
DeepSeek also faces pressure at home.
Chinese rivals include Moonshot’s Kimi and the GLM models from Z.ai, both competing for the same developer attention.
What this means
For developers, the calculation is straightforward.
If the benchmark claims hold up in real-world use, DeepSeek offers competitive coding performance at a much lower cost per task.
Free access to some search tools until November 1, 2026 lowers the barrier to experimenting further.
The caveat is that benchmarks are not production environments.
A 77.0% score on DeepSWE v1.1 is a meaningful data point, but teams will want to test reliability, security and compliance requirements against their own workloads before switching.
The things to watch are whether independent testing confirms DeepSeek’s benchmark numbers and how quickly developers adopt the new Search & Fetch APIs once the free period ends.

How these rankings are measured
What is measured
Each model is ranked by the number of tokens it processed through the OpenRouter API, counting both prompt and completion tokens.
Usage is aggregated into daily buckets in UTC and totalled per model variant, so variants of the same model, such as a free variant, are ranked separately.
Requests that a user or app keeps private are excluded before aggregation.
Selection period
Today, This Week, and This Month each cover a trailing window of one day, seven days, and thirty days, ending with the most recent complete daily bucket.
Trending compares the trailing seven days with the seven days before it and ranks models by the percentage change in tokens, including only models with at least one million tokens in the current window so that a small base cannot produce a large percentage.
New models with no prior week are listed first, up to five of them.
Freshness
The date above the rankings is the newest usage bucket the leaderboard is computed from, not the time the page was rendered or deployed, so it advances only when new usage data is aggregated.
How to read these rankings
These rankings show traffic routed through OpenRouter.
The Top Models chart and the LLM Leaderboard rank models by tokens processed, while the Market Share chart counts requests.
None of them measures users or spend.
Models differ in verbosity and tokenization, so a higher token total shows how much a model is used, not which model is best for a task.
They do not rank models by accuracy, reasoning ability, or benchmark performance.
The Benchmarks section ranks those using scores from Artificial Analysis and Design Arena, plus benchmarks such as GPQA Diamond that OpenRouter runs itself and reports as median accuracy across providers.
For coding, compare the Artificial Analysis Coding Index there with the Programming section, which ranks models by tokens on a sample of requests in a chosen language, such as Python.
The Top Models chart names the nine most-used models in each period and groups the rest as Others.
The Market Share chart shows each model author's share of text requests on OpenRouter, with the remaining authors grouped as Others.

2026年10月28日のCodex使用量リセットは、告知締め切りである日本時間16時より早い15時36分ごろに反映されました。画面上に表示された内容をもとに前回実績との比較や次回告知時に残枠を使い切るための行動基準を整理しています。なお、確認できたのは特定アカウントの画面のみであり、全プラン共通の挙動かは未確認です。
この記事の内容
Codexの使用量リセットは、2026年10月28日15時36分ごろに反映されました。告知されていた締め切り時刻（米太平洋夏時間基準で日本時間16時、標準時換算で17時）より24分早いタイミングです。前回の2026年10月25日も同じ「by midnight PST」の告知で、15時10分ごろに反映されており、2回続けて締め切りより前に利用枠が戻りました（経緯は前回の記事にまとめています）。
今後ふたたび「by midnight PST」というリセット告知が出た場合は、締め切り時刻の30分から1時間前までに残っている枠を使い切る判断が適しています。リセットが完了すると使用量の表示が0%付近に戻るため、残りの枠はリセット前に使うほうが得です。
ただし、今回の反映時刻は当サイトで運用している特定のアカウントにおいて、画面上に表示された内容を確認した結果です。すべてのプランや全利用者に対して同一の時刻に反映されたかどうかは未確認です。
2026年10月30日の追記：OpenAI の Codex 責任者が X で、Pro 100・Pro 200・Pro 500 などの利用制限を2倍にすると投稿しました。内訳や期間など、分かっていること・まだ分かっていないことはChatGPT Pro の利用制限が2倍に：Pro 200 は引き下げなし、対象プランと分かっていないことにまとめています。
この記事は 時点の情報です。情報が更新されている可能性があります。最新の情報は公式の発表で確認してください。
10月28日リセットの反映時刻と過去実績
2026年10月28日のリセットについて、告知から実際の反映までの流れと、直近の2026年10月25日の実績を比較した内容は以下の通りです。
| 実施日 | 告知内容 | 締め切り時刻（日本時間） | 実際の反映確認時刻（日本時間） |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026年10月25日 | by midnight PST（同じ告知） | 16:00（夏時間）/ 17:00（標準時） | 15:10ごろ（担当者が15:06に「行き渡った」と投稿） |
| 2026年10月28日 | Lands by midnight PST | 16:00（夏時間）/ 17:00（標準時） | 15:36ごろ |

「by midnight PST」が示す締め切り時刻と前倒しの傾向
告知文にある「by midnight PST」は、リセットが完了する締め切り時刻を示しています。米国では2026年11月1日まで夏時間（PDT、UTC-7）が適用されているため、告知が行われた米太平洋時間10月27日19時43分（PDT）から見た次の真夜中（10月28日0時00分PDT）は、日本時間の10月28日16時00分です。告知文の字面どおり太平洋標準時（PST、UTC-8）として解釈した場合は日本時間17時00分となります。
英語表現の「Lands by」は「その時刻までに完了して行き渡る」という意味であり、締め切り時刻ちょうどに処理が始まるわけではありません。過去2回の実績はいずれも締め切りの24分から50分ほど前に反映されています。ただし、これらは過去2回の手元での観察結果であり、次回以降も必ず前倒しされると保証されているわけではありません。

次に同様の告知が出された場合、締め切り時刻を待たずに手元の枠を消化する計画を立てる必要があります。リセットが完了すると使用量は0%付近に戻るため、残りの枠はリセット前に使うほうが得です。

- 告知された締め切りの30分から1時間前（日本時間15時00分から15時30分ごろ）を目安に、残っている使用枠を使い切る。

Is Tibo Still on Codex?
Reuters, Andrew Ambrosino and the Security Rumor
Tibo has not been publicly removed from Codex.
A Reuters report published November 3, 2026, says Thibault “Tibo” Sottiaux, the OpenAI executive who oversees product development, has recently taken charge of an internal initiative to secure OpenAI's systems.
Reuters attributes that to two people familiar with the matter.
It does not say he left Codex, lost a product role, or handed Codex to anyone else.
A viral post claiming that Andrew Ambrosino now “fully runs” Codex mixes that report with a joking X exchange and two details that do not check out.
Ambrosino did not announce the October 29 Pro limit increase; Tibo did.
Ambrosino's own CV lists no job at Apple.
Evidence reviewed November 4, 2026.
What Reuters actually reported
The Reuters story, by Deepa Seetharaman, is about something larger than one executive.
It describes years of internal warnings from OpenAI staff about operational security, from broad access to the company's main code repository to internal tools that were changed without regular security review.
The report was prompted in part by OpenAI's October disclosure that it had found a recording device planted in an executive conference room.
Tibo appears in the part of the story about how OpenAI is responding.
Reuters wrote that “Thibault Sottiaux, a senior executive overseeing product development, has recently taken charge of an internal initiative to secure OpenAI's internal systems,” citing two people familiar with the matter.
It added, citing one person, that in August Sottiaux “reassigned a quarter of OpenAI's production engineers to improve its security infrastructure.”
Three details in that wording matter for the Tibo Codex question:
- Reuters still describes him as the executive “overseeing product development.” That is a present-tense product role, not a past one.
- The security work is an “initiative” he has “taken charge of.” The report does not describe it as a new job title or a transfer out of product.
- The story does not mention Codex leadership, Andrew Ambrosino, or any change to who runs Codex day to day.
OpenAI did not confirm or deny the Tibo detail in the parts of its response that Reuters published.
A spokesperson said OpenAI is one of the most targeted organizations in the world and invests heavily in security.
After Reuters asked for comment, OpenAI pointed to a blog post about its next internal security sprint, covered below.
Is Tibo still in charge of Codex?
Based on public evidence, the best answer is that Tibo has not been publicly moved off Codex, and that his role was already broader than Codex before this week.
In May 2026, OpenAI reorganized its product teams under president Greg Brockman and combined ChatGPT, Codex and the API into one core product group, according to Wikipedia's entry on Sottiaux, which cites Wired's reporting at the time.
Sottiaux was put in charge of that group.
Since then, outlets have variously called him OpenAI's head of product, head of core products, and head of Codex and ChatGPT Work.
In other words, for about six months he has been the person above Codex, not only the person running it.
His recent public actions also point to an active role on the Codex side:
- On October 4 he launched a 28-day pledge to ship one clear improvement for Codex and ChatGPT Work users every day, or reset everyone's usage limits on days without one.
- On October 29 he posted that OpenAI was “doubling all usage limits for all Pro 100/200/500 tiers and Business Premium, effective today,” and canceling a planned cut to the Pro 200 allowance.
- When we checked his X profile on November 4, his bio read “Codex & ChatGPT @OpenAI.”
None of that rules out a change that has not been announced yet.
OpenAI has not published anything naming a new Codex lead, and it has not said that Tibo is stepping back from product.
Until it does, “Tibo was kicked off Codex” is a claim without a source.
Our reading: carrying a company-wide security push while running product is consistent with a senior executive being trusted with more, not less.
Pulling a quarter of production engineers onto security, as Reuters describes, is a decision that sits with someone who controls product engineering.
That is an inference from the reporting, not something OpenAI has stated.
Who is Andrew Ambrosino, and what does he run?
Andrew Ambrosino is a member of OpenAI's technical staff who leads product and engineering for the Codex desktop app, according to his own CV.
Before OpenAI, which he joined in 2025, he co-founded the fintech company Catch, where he served as CTO and CPO, and later led product at Noyo.
The CV lists earlier roles at MITRE, Microsoft and Upthere.
It does not list Apple.
His profile inside OpenAI has grown quickly.
A September 30 write-up of his TBPN interview said he had led the Codex desktop team since the app first shipped and had also taken on OpenAI's new Space product.
He presented at the July ChatGPT Work launch embedded above, and he has done several podcast interviews about the Codex app.
Some outlets have loosely called him “head of Codex” for months, which helps explain why a casual post from him this week was read as a promotion.
His X bio, checked November 4, reads “Codex & ChatGPT @OpenAI,” the same wording as Tibo's.
Neither bio shows a recent title change.
What the X exchange said, and what it did not
The viral screenshot is built around three posts.
Here they are in order, with times converted to Pacific time:
- Ambrosino, November 3, 5:38 p.m.: “starting today, you can now send me feedback for all the apps, not just OpenAI's.
hopefully this simplifies the feedback process for you all– you know I love a good merge”
- Tibo's reply, 10:23 p.m.: “Please make the model better, it doesn't yet do everything”
- Ambrosino's reply, 10:34 p.m.: “will get right on that”
Ambrosino's post had more than 440,000 views when we checked it.
It does not mention Codex, a new title, resets, Tibo, or security.
“You know I love a good merge” fits his public history of talking about merging Codex and ChatGPT, and OpenAI announced a merger of ChatGPT Chat and Work days earlier.
What “all the apps, not just OpenAI's” means exactly is unclear, and OpenAI has not explained it.
The Chinese-language post that spread the story translated Tibo's reply as roughly “make the model better, it's still far from good,” and described it as sour.
The English original is lighter.
“It doesn't yet do everything” reads most naturally as a joke playing on “all the apps”: if you are taking feedback on everything, make the model do everything.
Ambrosino's “will get right on that” reply matches that tone.
That is our interpretation of the wording; neither man has explained the exchange.
The viral claims, checked one by one
| Claim in the viral post | What the evidence shows | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Reuters reported Tibo moved to internal security | Reuters says he took charge of an internal security initiative, citing two people.
It still calls him the executive overseeing product development.
| Partly true |
| Tibo was kicked off the product front line | No source says this.
Reuters describes a current product role, and no OpenAI announcement says otherwise.
| Not supported |
| Ambrosino has fully taken over Codex | He leads the Codex desktop app.
No announcement names him head of all of Codex.
| Unconfirmed |
| Ambrosino now holds the “reset button” | No source says who controls usage resets after the 28-day pledge.
| Unconfirmed |
| Ambrosino doubled Pro limits days ago | Tibo posted the October 29 doubling, as reported by Android Authority and others.
| False |
| Ambrosino is a former Apple design lead | His CV lists MITRE, Microsoft, Upthere, Catch and Noyo.
No Apple role.
| Not supported |
| Tibo's reply was a sour parting shot | The reply is real.
“Sour” comes from a harsher translation and the poster's reading.
| Misleading |
